subject.title: fix(embeddings): bound openai-compatible requests without AbortSignal

question: Should every unsignaled OpenAI-compatible embedding call adopt fixed 60-second query and 120-second batch deadlines, or should only the gateway and capability-CLI entry points own those deadlines?
rationale: Both policies prevent the reported hang, but only maintainers can define whether the generic provider may terminate previously successful slow self-hosted requests without an existing configuration override.

options.title: Keep deadlines caller-owned
options.body: Add explicit deadlines at the gateway and capability-CLI entry points or propagate an existing embedding budget so unrelated provider callers retain their current latency behavior.

options.title: Adopt provider-wide floors
options.body: Confirm 60 and 120 seconds as the supported generic provider contract and require slow-success upgrade proof plus user-visible release context before merge.

options.title: Use a conservative safety cap
options.body: Apply a substantially larger provider-wide hang cap derived from established maximum embedding policy to bound dead sockets without targeting normal slow local workloads.

recommendation.title: Keep deadlines caller-owned
recommendation.body: Add explicit deadlines at the gateway and capability-CLI entry points or propagate an existing embedding budget so unrelated provider callers retain their current latency behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person most directly to embedding-provider refactors and the surrounding provider/config runtime boundary.
